doc.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021

chapter: Sun Ra's last years and the estate
title: Alton Abraham and the satchel of masters
summary: Gordon describes Abraham as a mystery figure who stayed in Chicago and delivered masters in a battered satchel.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah, we had a warm, I had a warm relationship with Alton Abraham. He was a really great guy. He is — was — the real, the real mystery figure. There was little mention of him and he was a very nice guy.
Did he, did he, I know he moved, well he must have moved from Chicago. Did he relocate in Sun Ra’s wake as Sun Ra moved around?
Oh so he was still in Chicago.

The first, I remember he flew into Philly and had like a leather satchel, like kind of beat up, and he had masters in there and he flew into Philly and he came to our office and he just gave us the satchel and left the satchel there. And I never got rid of it it was just like another holy Sun Ra artifact, this beat up satchel that he brought the masters in and he just left it there, you know, “Here.”
